machine_action_rules: Treat only source_latin as editable Interslavic language canon.
Never edit source_cyrillic as an independent translation; regenerate it from authenticated Latin sources.
Do not edit the German authority from this language lane.
Append a source-pinned decision with evidence and rejected alternatives for every material linguistic change.
Preserve mathematics, TeX syntax, complete foreign identities, citations, and reviewed Roman structures according to the role inventory.
After a Latin change: replay/verify the ledger, rerun the completeness audit, derive Cyrillic, build both scripts serially, then rerun text/math/font/visual QA.
Do not claim native-speaker, community, official-standard, or scholarly-peer-review certification without an authentic receipt.

claim_boundaries.review: no independent native-speaker/community/scholarly peer review claimed
claim_boundaries.cyrillic: deterministic representation of Latin Interslavic, not independent evidence
claim_boundaries.rights: CC0 only to the extent rights exist in project-created translation, editorial work, metadata, manifests, tools, and evidence; third-party material retains its own status
